questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding thrombi, except:

options.label: A
options.text: Arterial/ cardiac thrombi form at the sight of turbulence or endothelial injury

options.label: B
options.text: Thrombi are focally attached to the point of initiation

options.label: C
options.text: Arterial Thrombi propagate away from the heart

options.label: D
options.text: Venous Thrombi are formed due to stasis and extend in the direction of blood flow

questions.answerText: Arterial Thrombi propagate away from the heart
questions.solutionHtml:
Arterial Thrombi propagate away from the heart.
  • Arterial thrombi tend to grow retrograde, i.e. they propagate towards the heart.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 125, 126, 128

questions.stem: False statement regarding lines of Zahn is-

options.label: A
options.text: Lines of Zahn are seen grossly and microscopically

options.label: B
options.text: These signify antemortem clot

options.label: C
options.text: These have alternate deposits of pale platelet, fibrin and RBC deposition

options.label: D
options.text: Laminations signify that a thrombus is formed due to stasis

questions.answerText: Laminations signify that a thrombus is formed due to stasis
questions.solutionHtml:
Laminations signify that a thrombus is formed due to stasis
  • Thrombi often have grossly and microscopically apparent laminations called lines of Zahn, pale platelet and fibrin deposits alternating with darker red cell–rich layers.
  • Such laminations signify that a thrombus has formed in flowing blood. Their presence can therefore distinguish antemortem clots from the bland non-laminated clots that occur post-mortem. Post-mortem clots have a Chicken fat appearance due to the settlement of RBcs under the fact layer.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 125, 126, 128

questions.stem: All statements are true regarding arterial thrombi except:

options.label: A
options.text: These are frequently occlusive

options.label: B
options.text: These consist of platelets, fibrin RBC and degenerated leukocytes

options.label: C
options.text: Cerebral artery is the most common to be involved

options.label: D
options.text: These are superimposed on the rupture of atherosclerotic plaques or vascular injury

questions.answerText: Cerebral artery is the most common to be involved
questions.solutionHtml:
Cerebral artery is the most common to be involved
  • Arterial thrombi are frequently occlusive.
  • The most common sites in decreasing order of frequency are the coronary, cerebral, and femoral arteries.
  • They typically consist of a friable meshwork of platelets, fibrin, red cells, and degenerating leukocytes.
  • Although these are usually superimposed on a ruptured atherosclerotic plaque, other vascular injuries like vasculitis, and trauma may as well be the underlying cause.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 128Module Name - HEMODYNAMIC DISORDERS THROMBOEMBOLIC DISEASE & SHOCK - Morphology Of Thrombosis

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding post-mortem clots except

options.label: A
options.text: Gelatinous in nature

options.label: B
options.text: Attached to the underlying vessel

options.label: C
options.text: It can sometimes be confused with antemortem venous thrombi

options.label: D
options.text: Upper part is yellow, while the lower part is dark red

questions.solutionHtml:
Attached to the underlying vessel
  • Postmortem clots can sometimes be mistaken for Antemortem Venous Thrombi.
  • However, clots that form after death are gelatinous and have a dark red dependent portion where red cells have settled by gravity and a yellow “chicken fat” upper portion and are usually NOT attached to the underlying vessel wall.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 125, 126, 128

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding DVT, except:

options.label: A
options.text: DVT can embolise the lungs

options.label: B
options.text: 50% of the cases are usually asymptomatic

options.label: C
options.text: It usually involves a large leg vein at or above the knee

options.label: D
options.text: Bed rest helps in the prevention of DVT

questions.answerText: Bed rest helps in the prevention of DVT
questions.solutionHtml:
Bed rest helps in the prevention of DVT
  • Prolonged Bed rest predisposes to Deep Vein Thrombosis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 130
